figures.alt: Illustration of a grandmother and a child sitting in the shade of a striped beach umbrella on a sandy lake beach.
figures.caption: A beach umbrella makes shade, so the sand under it stays cooler.

figures.alt: Illustration of two children in winter coats and boots building a snowman in a snowy front yard, away from the street, while snow falls.
figures.caption: Snow falls in Michigan winters. We dress warm and play away from the road.

figures.alt: Photo of two ice cubes in small metal trays on a sunny windowsill. One has a small paper shade held up by a craft stick. The other is uncovered.
figures.caption: The finished Sun-Safe Beach Helper test: one shaded ice cube, one uncovered control, same window.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Weather over 20 days (Michigan fall sample). Sunny 8 days, Cloudy 6 days, Rainy 4 days, Snowy 2 days.
figures.caption: A 20-day Michigan fall sample: 8 sunny, 6 cloudy, 4 rainy and 2 snowy days. Sunny days were the most common.

figures.alt: Bar graph, Melt drops after the same time. Shaded ice 5 drops, Uncovered ice 12 drops.
figures.caption: The ice cube in the shade left 5 drops of melt. The ice cube in the sun left 12 drops.
